Single taps are simple discrete motor executions with no strong evidence of engaging executive programming in the fMRI results (study notes medial frontal activation was not significant for discrete movements). GLOBAL_I2 (relevance to executive function) is not met; local POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I1 (task measures executive function) is also not met.

Task is a simple motor tapping task, not a working memory task. Missing WORKING_MEMORY_I1 (task measures working memory) and WORKING_MEMORY_I2 (contrast measures working-memory-related activation). Additionally, GLOBAL_I2 (relevance to executive function/cognitive control) is not clearly met for discrete taps.

Single taps do not measure inhibitory control (no Go/No-Go or stop paradigm). Missing INHIBITION_I1 (task measures inhibitory control) and INHIBITION_I2 (contrast measures inhibition-related activation); GLOBAL_I2 is not clearly met for discrete taps.

Single taps do not involve task- or rule-switching. Missing COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I1 (task measures cognitive flexibility) and COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I2 (contrast measures flexibility-related activation); GLOBAL_I2 is not clearly met for discrete taps.

Single discrete tapping is simple motor execution rather than a planning task (e.g., Tower of London). Missing PLANNING_I1 (task measures planning) and PLANNING_I2 (contrast measures planning-related activation); GLOBAL_I2 not clearly met.

Single-tap trials do not assess sustained attention/vigilance. Missing VIGILANCE_I1 (task measures vigilance) and VIGILANCE_I2 (contrast measures vigilance-related activation); GLOBAL_I2 not clearly met.

Although initiation behavior (reaction time) can be assessed behaviorally, the discrete single-tap fMRI contrast did not show medial frontal initiation-related activation and does not clearly index initiation programming in the imaging data. Missing INITIATION_I2 (contrast specifically measuring initiation-related activation); GLOBAL_I2 (relevance to executive control in the imaging contrast) is not clearly met for discrete taps.

Sequential (four-tap) trains require programming/sequence generation and the fMRI contrast shows medial and dorsolateral premotor activations associated with sequencing, consistent with task-related executive control. Meets GLOBAL_I1 (group-level whole-brain task activation), GLOBAL_I2 (relevant to executive function), and local POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I1 and POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I2 (task measures executive sequencing/programming and contrast is task-related).

Sequential tapping is a motor sequencing task, not a working-memory task. Missing WORKING_MEMORY_I1 (task measures working memory) and WORKING_MEMORY_I2 (contrast measures working-memory-related activation).

Sequences of taps do not operationalize inhibitory-control paradigms (e.g., Go/No-Go, Stop-signal). Missing INHIBITION_I1 (task measures inhibitory control) and INHIBITION_I2 (contrast measures inhibition-related activation).

The sequential tapping task does not require task- or rule-switching as in cognitive-flexibility paradigms. Missing COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I1 (task measures cognitive flexibility) and COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I2 (contrast measures flexibility-related activation).

Although sequencing involves organization of actions, this task is a repetitive motor-sequencing paradigm rather than a formal planning task (e.g., Tower of London). Missing PLANNING_I1 (task measures planning) and PLANNING_I2 (contrast measures planning-related activation).
The four-tap sequence is not a sustained-attention/vigilance paradigm. Missing VIGILANCE_I1 (task measures vigilance) and VIGILANCE_I2 (contrast measures vigilance-related activation).

Sequential tapping engages programming/initiation of trains of responses; behavioral results reported initiation deficits for sequences in patients and the fMRI shows medial frontal activation during sequential (but not discrete) movements, indicating initiation-related neural activity. Meets GLOBAL_I1 (group whole-brain task activation), GLOBAL_I2 (relevance to initiation/executive control), and local INITIATION_I1 and INITIATION_I2 (task measures action initiation/programming and contrast shows initiation-related activation for sequences).
